model_original_and_bound_product_receipt.original_model_findings_or_planner_reaso:
Continue high and prune low. On the original low grid, x = (0, 0.5, 1) scored (−4, −2.25, −1). On the original high grid, x = (1.5, 1.75, 2.5) scored (−0.25, −0.0625, −0.25). With the inclusive cutoff of −0.25, 0 of 3 low points and 3 of 3 high points qualified. This supports H_high and refutes H_low on the specified finite grids. The original observations and evaluations agree with the independent assessment (gxa_01m84gjg5h2701jnn6, gxa_01m84gjgcc70krm764, gxa_01m84gjg762nmp3n4t, gxa_01m84gjgda60hagv89, gxa_01m84gm071rgp19fnk).

The unique quadratic through the three high observations is q(x) = −(x − 2)². The piecewise-linear interpolant has slope 0.75 up to x = 1.75 and −0.25 thereafter. At catalog coordinates (1.625, 1.8125, 2.125, 2.375), the respective predicted scores are (−0.140625, −0.03515625, −0.015625, −0.140625) for the quadratic and (−0.15625, −0.078125, −0.15625, −0.21875) for the piecewise-linear fit. Their maxima select x = 2.125 for 'quadratic' and x = 1.8125 for 'linear'. Measure both in one grid, compare their observed scores, then close. One held-out choice per method can establish which choice scored higher on this fixture. General method performance and scores at the other catalog coordinates remain unresolved.
